prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone in St. Louis — the right choice depends on your home, budget, timeline, and the level of finish you want. I can help you pick the best one for your situation. Below are practical steps, what to look for, and how to narrow it to the best company for your job.

How to find the best interior painter for you
- Get at least 3 written estimates so you can compare scope, materials, prep work, and timeline.
- Check recent reviews and photos on Google, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, Houzz, BBB, and Nextdoor.
- Ask for references for similar jobs (same size room, trim level, and whether they did texture/repair work).
- Confirm license/insurance and ask for proof of general liability and workers’ comp.
- Look at their portfolio for quality, edge work, and color consistency.

Key questions to ask a painter
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see proof?
- Do you provide a written estimate and contract? What’s included (prep, caulking, drywall repair, priming, number of coats)?
- What paint brands and products do you recommend? Do you use low-VOC options?
- Who will do the work (company crew or subs)? Who will be on-site?
- What is the timeframe and estimated completion date?
- What is your warranty or touch-up policy?
- Can you provide references from local projects in the last 6–12 months?

What to include in the contract
- Detailed scope (rooms, surfaces, number of coats, sheen)
- Paint brand/finish and color codes
- Prep work (moving furniture, wall repair, sanding, priming)
- Start and finish dates, daily working hours
- Total price and deposit schedule
- Cleanup and disposal terms
- Warranty/touch-up terms

Red flags
- Extremely low estimate compared to others with no explanation
- No written contract or unwillingness to provide proof of insurance
- Poor or nonexistent references or no recent photos of finished work
- Pressure to pay large upfront deposits in cash

Where to look locally
- Google Maps/Google Reviews
- Yelp
- Angi (Angie’s List) / HomeAdvisor
- Houzz
- BBB and Nextdoor for neighborhood recommendations

Would you like me to:
- Draft a short message/email you can send to painters asking the right questions?
- Help you narrow options if you tell me your ZIP code, number of rooms, and whether you need drywall repair or special finishes?

Tell me which of those you want and I’ll prepare it.
